data.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService
data.description:
Blueprint service exposed directly to Python.

This service provides blueprint introspection and analysis with native
Unreal Engine types.

Python Usage:
  import unreal

  # Get blueprint info (returns BlueprintDetailedInfo or None)
  info = unreal.BlueprintService.get_blueprint_info("/Game/Blueprints/BP_Player_Test")
  if info:
      print(f"Parent: {info.parent_class}")
      for var in info.variables:
          print(f"  {var.variable_name}: {var.variable_type}")

  # List variables
  variables = unreal.BlueprintService.list_variables("/Game/BP_Player_Test")

  # List components
  components = unreal.BlueprintService.list_components("/Game/BP_Player_Test")

@note All methods are static and thread-safe
@note C++ out parameters become Python return values

tools.description: Check if a variable exists in a blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.VariableExists

returnValue.description: True if variable exists Example: if not unreal.BlueprintService.variable_exists(bp_path, "Health"): unreal.BlueprintService.add_member_variable(bp_path, "Health", "float")

tools.description: Update a local variable in a function.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.UpdateFunctionLocalVariable

variableName.description: Current name of the local variable

newName.description: New name for the variable (empty to keep current)

newType.description: New type for the variable (empty to keep current)

newDefaultValue.description: New default value (empty to keep current)

returnValue.description: True if successful Example - Rename local variable: unreal.BlueprintService.update_function_local_variable("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage", "TempVar", NewName="FinalDamage") Example - Change type: unreal.BlueprintService.update_function_local_variable("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage", "Counter", NewType="int64")

tools.description:
Split a struct pin into individual member pins.
Works on struct types like FVector, FRotator, FTransform, etc.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SplitPin

pinName.description: Name of the struct pin to split

returnValue.description: True if successful Example - Split a Vector output: unreal.BlueprintService.split_pin("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", node_id, "ReturnValue") # Now you can connect to ReturnValue_X, ReturnValue_Y, ReturnValue_Z

tools.description: Set the default value of an existing variable.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SetVariableDefaultValue

defaultValue.description: New default value as a string

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: unreal.BlueprintService.set_variable_default_value("/Game/BP_Player", "Health", "150.0")

tools.description:
Set a component as the root component of the blueprint.
The component must be a SceneComponent and must exist in the blueprint.
The previous root's children are reparented to the new root. If the previous root was
the auto-generated DefaultSceneRoot it is removed entirely (matching the Blueprint
editor); a previous user-created root becomes a child of the new root. Any other
root-level scene components are also folded under the new root, since an actor has
exactly one scene root.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SetRootComponent

componentName.description: Name of the component to make root

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: unreal.BlueprintService.set_root_component("/Game/BP_Player", "MyNewRoot")

tools.description:
Set a property value on a blueprint's Class Default Object (CDO).
WARNING: Modifying CDO can cause instability. Prefer using variables and defaults instead.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SetProperty

propertyName.description: Name of the property to set

propertyValue.description: Value to set as a string

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: unreal.BlueprintService.set_property("/Game/BP_Player", "Health", "150.0")

tools.description:
Set the position of a node in a graph.
Use this to reposition Entry/Result nodes for clean layouts.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SetNodePosition

nodeId.description: GUID of the node to reposition

posX.description: New X position in the graph

posY.description: New Y position in the graph

returnValue.description: True if successful Example - Reposition Result node to end of function: unreal.BlueprintService.set_node_position("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage", result_id, 800, 0) Example - Separate stacked Entry/Result nodes: nodes = unreal.BlueprintService.get_nodes_in_graph(path, func) for node in nodes: if "FunctionEntry" in node.node_type: unreal.BlueprintService.set_node_position(path, func, node.node_id, 0, 0) elif "FunctionResult" in node.node_type: unreal.BlueprintService.set_node_position(path, func, node.node_id, 800, 0)

tools.description: Set a pin's default value on a node.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SetNodePinValue

pinName.description: Name of the pin to set

returnValue.description: True if successful Example - Set string value: unreal.BlueprintService.set_node_pin_value("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", node_id, "InString", "Hello World") Example - Set numeric value: unreal.BlueprintService.set_node_pin_value("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage", node_id, "B", "2.5")

tools.description: Set a property value on a component in a blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SetComponentProperty

propertyName.description: Name of the property to set

propertyValue.description: Value to set as a string

returnValue.description: True if successful Example - Set relative location: unreal.BlueprintService.set_component_property("/Game/BP_Player", "Mesh", "RelativeLocation", "(X=0,Y=0,Z=50)") Example - Set visibility: unreal.BlueprintService.set_component_property("/Game/BP_Player", "Mesh", "bVisible", "true")

tools.description:
Set collision settings on a primitive component in a blueprint.

Collision properties live inside UPrimitiveComponent::BodyInstance and cannot be set
via set_component_property (which only resolves top-level properties). Use this method
to configure collision profile, enabled state, object type, and per-channel responses.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SetCollisionSettings

componentName.description: Name of the component (must be a UPrimitiveComponent)

channelResponses.description: Map of channel name -> response: "Ignore", "Overlap", "Block" (empty map = no change)

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: unreal.BlueprintService.set_collision_settings( "/Game/BP_Cube", "CollisionSphere", collision_enabled="QueryOnly", object_type="WorldDynamic", collision_profile="Custom", channel_responses={"Pawn": "Overlap", "WorldStatic": "Ignore", "WorldDynamic": "Ignore"})

tools.description:
Search for available variable types.
Use this to discover valid type names/paths before creating variables.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.SearchVariableTypes

searchTerm.description: Search term to filter types (partial match, case-insensitive)

returnValue.description: Array of matching type information Example - Search for Vector types: types = unreal.BlueprintService.search_variable_types("Vector") for t in types: print(f"{t.type_name}: {t.type_path}") Example - Get all Structure types: types = unreal.BlueprintService.search_variable_types("", "Structure")

tools.description:
Refresh/reconstruct a node to update its pins and connections.
Useful after modifying a function signature or when pins are out of date.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.RefreshNode

nodeId.description: GUID of the node to refresh

bCompile.description: Whether to compile the blueprint after refresh (default: true)

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: unreal.BlueprintService.refresh_node("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", node_id)

tools.description: Recombine a previously split pin back into a single struct pin.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.RecombinePin

pinName.description: Base name of the split pin to recombine

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: unreal.BlueprintService.recombine_pin("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", node_id, "ReturnValue")

tools.description:
Override a parent-class BlueprintImplementableEvent or BlueprintNativeEvent.
Equivalent to selecting a function from the "Override" dropdown in the editor.

Automatically chooses the correct mechanism:
  - Functions with FUNC_Event (void/latent — EnterState, StateCompleted, Tick etc.)
    → adds an event node to the EventGraph (same as add_event_node)
  - Functions that return a value (GetDescription etc.)
    → creates a function graph with entry + result nodes

Idempotent — safe to call if the override already exists.

After calling this:
  - Event-style: use get_nodes_in_graph(bp_path, "EventGraph") to find the node
  - Function-style: use get_nodes_in_graph(bp_path, function_name) to find entry/result
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.OverrideFunction

functionName.description: Exact name as returned by list_overridable_functions (case-sensitive)

returnValue.description: True if the override was created (or already existed) Example — function with return value: unreal.BlueprintService.override_function(bp, "ReceiveGetDescription") nodes = unreal.BlueprintService.get_nodes_in_graph(bp, "ReceiveGetDescription") Example — event style: unreal.BlueprintService.override_function(bp, "ReceiveLatentEnterState") nodes = unreal.BlueprintService.get_nodes_in_graph(bp, "EventGraph")

tools.description:
Open a blueprint and navigate to a specific function graph.
Opens the blueprint editor and focuses on the specified function tab.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.OpenFunctionGraph

functionName.description: Name of the function to open (use "EventGraph" for main graph)

returnValue.description: True if successful Example - Open a function graph: unreal.BlueprintService.open_function_graph("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage") Example - Open the EventGraph: unreal.BlueprintService.open_function_graph("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph")

tools.description: Check if a node with the given title exists in a graph.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.NodeExists

graphName.description: Name of the graph ("EventGraph", function name, etc.)

returnValue.description: True if a node with matching title exists Example: if not unreal.BlueprintService.node_exists(bp_path, "EventGraph", "Event BeginPlay"): # Add BeginPlay event

tools.description:
Modify settings on an existing timeline. Pass a sentinel to leave a setting unchanged:
empty string for NewName, a negative number for Length, and -1 for the int flags
(0 = false, 1 = true).
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ModifyTimeline

newName.description: New name (also renames the component variable & event-track functions), or "" to leave

length.description: New fixed length in seconds, or < 0 to leave

useLastKeyFrame.description: 1 = length follows last keyframe, 0 = fixed length, -1 = leave

returnValue.description: True if the timeline was found and (any) change applied Example: unreal.BlueprintService.modify_timeline("/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube", "LookAtTimeline", "", 0.75, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1)

tools.description:
Modify an existing input parameter on a Custom Event node — rename it, change its type, or both.
Existing connections are preserved where the change allows (a rename keeps wires; a type change
keeps wires only if the new type is compatible).
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ModifyCustomEventInput

graphName.description: Name of the graph containing the node

nodeId.description: GUID of the Custom Event node

parameterName.description: Current name of the input pin to modify

newName.description: New name for the pin, or empty to keep the current name

newType.description: New type string (same type-string format as add_function_local_variable), or empty to keep the current type

bIsArray.description: Whether the new type is an array (only used when NewType is provided)

containerType.description: Container type for the new type: "Array", "Set", "Map", or empty (only used when NewType is provided)

returnValue.description: True if the pin was found and modified Example: unreal.BlueprintService.modify_custom_event_input("/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube", "EventGraph", node_id, "Rotation", "TargetRotation", "FRotator")

tools.description: Check if a local variable exists in a function.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.LocalVariableExists

returnValue.description: True if local variable exists Example: if not unreal.BlueprintService.local_variable_exists(bp_path, "ApplyDamage", "TempValue"): unreal.BlueprintService.add_function_local_variable(bp_path, "ApplyDamage", "TempValue", "float")

tools.description: List all variables in a blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ListVariables

returnValue.description: Array of variable information Example: vars = unreal.BlueprintService.list_variables("/Game/BP_Player_Test") for var in vars: print(f"{var.variable_name}: {var.variable_type}")

tools.description:
List all functions from the parent class hierarchy that can be overridden
in this blueprint (BlueprintImplementableEvent / BlueprintNativeEvent).
Each entry reports whether the override already exists in this blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ListOverridableFunctions

functionName.description: Function name (also the graph name when overridden)

ownerClass.description: C++ class that declares the function (e.g. "StateTreeTaskBlueprintBase")

bAlreadyOverridden.description: Whether this function is already overridden in this blueprint

bIsNativeEvent.description: True for BlueprintNativeEvent (has C++ default), false for BlueprintImplementableEvent

bIsEventStyle.description:
True if this override should be created as an event node in the EventGraph
(void/latent functions with FUNC_Event flag — e.g. EnterState, StateCompleted, Tick).
False if it should be a function graph with a return node (e.g. GetDescription).
override_function() uses this automatically — no need to check manually.

parameters.description: Parameter names and types as "Name:Type" strings

returnValue.description: Array of overridable function info Example: funcs = unreal.BlueprintService.list_overridable_functions("/Game/StateTree/STT_Rotate") for f in funcs: print(f"{f.function_name} ({f.owner_class}) overridden={f.already_overridden}")

tools.description:
Enumerate every UEdGraph attached to a Blueprint — ubergraph pages, functions,
macros, and delegate signature graphs.

Use this when you don't know the exact name of a graph tab. The default
Blueprint editor only exposes "EventGraph" by name; user-created ubergraph
pages (e.g. "Graph_PlayerInput") and inherited function graphs are invisible
without this enumeration.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ListGraphs

graphName.description: Tab name as shown in the My Blueprint panel (e.g. "EventGraph", "Graph_PlayerInput", "MyFunction")

nodeCount.description: Number of nodes in this graph (cheap to compute, useful as a sanity signal)

returnValue.description: Array of FBlueprintGraphInfo, one per graph Example: graphs = unreal.BlueprintService.list_graphs("/Game/Blueprints/BP_Player_Test") for g in graphs: print(f"{g.graph_kind:20}  {g.graph_name:30}  ({g.node_count} nodes)")

tools.description: List all functions in a blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ListFunctions

returnValue.description: Array of function information Example: funcs = unreal.BlueprintService.list_functions("/Game/BP_Player_Test")

tools.description: List all local variables in a function.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ListFunctionLocalVariables

returnValue.description: Array of local variable information Example: locals = unreal.BlueprintService.list_function_local_variables("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage") for var in locals: print(f"{var.variable_name}: {var.variable_type} = {var.default_value}")

tools.description: List all components in a blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ListComponents

bIsInherited.description:
True if this component comes from a parent C++ class and cannot be removed via Python APIs.
These are the "grayed out" components shown in the Blueprint Editor Components panel.
To replace an inherited root (e.g. DefaultSceneRoot), call set_root_component() instead.

returnValue.description: Array of component information Example: comps = unreal.BlueprintService.list_components("/Game/BP_Player_Test")

tools.description:
List all properties of a component in a blueprint.
This is an alias for GetAllComponentProperties with a more intuitive name.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.ListComponentProperties

bIncludeInherited.description: Whether to include inherited properties (default: true)

returnValue.description: Array of property information Example: props = unreal.BlueprintService.list_component_properties("/Game/BP_Player", "Mesh") for prop in props: print(f"{prop.property_name}: {prop.property_type} = {prop.value}")

tools.description: Check if a blueprint is a Widget Blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.IsWidgetBlueprint

returnValue.description: True if it's a Widget Blueprint Example: is_widget = unreal.BlueprintService.is_widget_blueprint("/Game/UI/WBP_MainMenu")

tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific variable.
Use this to discover all properties that can be modified before calling ModifyVariable.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetVariableInfo

outInfo.title: BlueprintVariableDetailedInfo
outInfo.description: Detailed variable information (C++ only, becomes return value in Python)

bIsInstanceEditable.description: Whether the variable can be edited per instance in Details panel

bIsExposeOnSpawn.description: Whether the variable is exposed on spawn

bIsBlueprintReadOnly.description: Whether the variable is read-only in Blueprints

bIsExposeToCinematics.description: Whether the variable is exposed to cinematics/Sequencer

bIsArray.description: Whether this is an array type

bIsSet.description: Whether this is a set type

bIsMap.description: Whether this is a map type

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: info = unreal.BlueprintService.get_variable_info("/Game/BP_Player", "Health")  # BlueprintVariableDetailedInfo or None if info: print(f"Type: {info.variable_type}, Category: {info.category}") print(f"Replication: {info.replication_condition}")

tools.description: List the timelines on a blueprint, with their float track names.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetTimelines

returnValue.description: Array of "TimelineName" entries; each entry's ParameterType lists comma-separated float track names Example: for t in unreal.BlueprintService.get_timelines("/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube"): print(t.parameter_name, "tracks:", t.parameter_type)

tools.description:
Get the nodes currently selected by the user in an open Blueprint editor.

Reads the live selection from FBlueprintEditor::GetSelectedNodes(). The
Blueprint must already be open in the editor (graph selection only exists
on the open Slate panel — there is no persisted selection state on the
asset itself). Use this to act on whatever the user has highlighted in
the graph (e.g. inspect, reposition, document, or programmatically edit
the selected nodes).
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetSelectedNodes

blueprintPath.description: Full path to the blueprint. If empty, the first open Blueprint editor with a non-empty selection is used (handy when the agent doesn't yet know which asset the user is looking at).

bIsInput.description: exec, bool, float, int, string, object, etc.

bIsConnected.description: True for input, false for output

pins.description: Names of all pins on this node (for quick reference)

returnValue.description: Array of node information for the currently selected graph nodes. The array is empty if no Blueprint editor is open, the asset isn't open, or nothing is selected. The graph the selection belongs to can be inferred from the focused graph; callers that need the graph name explicitly should pair this with get_nodes_in_graph. Example: selected = unreal.BlueprintService.get_selected_nodes("/Game/BP_Player") for n in selected: print(f"selected: {n.node_title} ({n.node_type})

tools.description: Get a property value from a blueprint's Class Default Object (CDO).
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetProperty

propertyName.description: Name of the property to get

outValue.description: Property value as a string (C++ only, becomes return value in Python)

returnValue.description: True if successful Python Usage — bool + out param collapse into ONE return value (str or None, NOT a tuple): value = unreal.BlueprintService.get_property("/Game/BP_Player", "Health")   # e.g. "150.0", or None if not found Use the native C++ property name: booleans KEEP the 'b' prefix here ("bReplicates"), unlike Python attribute access which strips it. Values come back as strings ("True"/"False").

tools.description: Get the parent class of a blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetParentClass

returnValue.description: Parent class name, or empty string if not found Example: parent = unreal.BlueprintService.get_parent_class("/Game/BP_Player_Test")

tools.description:
Get all nodes in a graph.

On large graphs the full dump is expensive — prefer get_graph_summary first,
then narrow this call with the optional filters.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetNodesInGraph

nameFilter.description: Case-insensitive substring match against node title, node type, or node id; empty = all nodes

bIncludePins.description: False drops the pins/pin_names arrays (the bulk of the payload) leaving id/type/title/position per node

bIsInput.description: exec, bool, float, int, string, object, etc.

bIsConnected.description: True for input, false for output

pins.description: Names of all pins on this node (for quick reference)

returnValue.description: Array of node information Example: nodes = unreal.BlueprintService.get_nodes_in_graph("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage") for node in nodes: print(f"{node.node_title} at ({node.pos_x}, {node.pos_y})") Example - terse read of just the SpawnActor nodes, no pin data: nodes = unreal.BlueprintService.get_nodes_in_graph("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", 25, "SpawnActor", False)

tools.description: Get detailed pin information for a specific node.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetNodePins

bIsInput.description: exec, bool, float, int, string, object, etc.

bIsConnected.description: True for input, false for output

returnValue.description: Array of pin information Example: pins = unreal.BlueprintService.get_node_pins("/Game/BP_Player", "ApplyDamage", "45CC026642D99D1D713EDCA5C483E490") for pin in pins: print(f"{pin.pin_name} ({pin.pin_type}) - {'input' if pin.is_input else 'output'}")

tools.description:
Get detailed information about a specific node in a graph.
Returns complete pin information including connections.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetNodeDetails

graphName.description: Graph name this node belongs to

bIsPure.description: Whether this is a pure node (no exec pins)

bIsLatent.description: Whether this node has latent execution

functionName.description: For function calls: target function name

pinCategory.description: Pin type category (exec, bool, float, int, string, object, struct, etc.)

pinSubCategory.description: Pin type subcategory or object/struct path

typePath.description: Full type path for struct/object types

bIsInput.description: Whether this is an input pin

bIsArray.description: Whether this is an array type

bIsReference.description: Whether this is a reference type

bCanSplit.description: Whether the pin can be split (struct pins)

bIsSplit.description: Whether the pin is currently split

connections.description: Connected node IDs and pin names (format: "NodeId:PinName")

pinCategory.description: Pin type category (exec, bool, float, int, string, object, struct, etc.)

pinSubCategory.description: Pin type subcategory or object/struct path

typePath.description: Full type path for struct/object types

bIsInput.description: Whether this is an input pin

bIsArray.description: Whether this is an array type

bIsReference.description: Whether this is a reference type

bCanSplit.description: Whether the pin can be split (struct pins)

bIsSplit.description: Whether the pin is currently split

connections.description: Connected node IDs and pin names (format: "NodeId:PinName")

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: info = unreal.BlueprintService.get_node_details("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", node_id)  # detailed info struct or None if info: for pin in info.input_pins: print(f"  {pin.pin_name}: {pin.pin_category}")

tools.description:
Get a fixed-size overview of a graph: node/connection counts, blueprint
compile status, entry points, and a node-class histogram. Use this as the
default first read on any graph — its payload does not grow with graph
size, unlike get_nodes_in_graph.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.GetGraphSummary

outSummary.title: BlueprintGraphSummary
outSummary.description: Filled with the summary on success

graphName.description: Tab name as shown in the My Blueprint panel

connectionCount.description: Number of pin-to-pin links in the graph

compileStatus.description: Blueprint-level compile status: UpToDate | UpToDateWithWarnings | Dirty | Error | Unknown

entryPoints.description: Titles of entry-point nodes (events, custom events, function entry) with their node ids: "Title|NodeId"

nodeTypeCounts.description: Node class histogram, most frequent first: "K2Node_CallFunction x12"

returnValue.description: True if the blueprint and graph were found Example: s = unreal.BlueprintService.get_graph_summary("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph") if s[0]: print(s[1].node_count, s[1].compile_status, s[1].entry_points)

tools.description:
Get the definition of an existing graph in the batch builder format.
The returned definition can be fed back into BuildGraph.
Enables round-tripping and learning from hand-built graphs.

Python Usage:
  success, nodes, connections, defaults, error = \
      unreal.BlueprintService.get_graph_definition("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph")

tools.description:
Create multiple nodes, wire connections, and set pin defaults in a single
call. The entire operation is wrapped in FScopedTransaction (Ctrl+Z undoes all).

Uses the same discovery/spawner resolution as individual methods.
Every connection goes through Schema->TryCreateConnection().
Nodes that fail to create are skipped (with errors logged).
Connections referencing failed nodes are skipped.
The graph is left in a valid state regardless of partial failures.

Python Usage:
  result = unreal.BlueprintService.build_graph(
      "/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph",
      [{"ref":"BeginPlay", "type":"event", "params":{"event":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}},
       {"ref":"Print", "type":"print_string", "params":{}}],
      [{"from_":"BeginPlay.then", "to":"Print.execute"}],
      [{"node_ref":"Print", "pin_name":"InString", "value":"Hello!"}],
      True, True)

  Note: Connection refs can be local refs (from Nodes array) or existing node GUIDs.
  Note: Use "from_" (with underscore) because "from" is a Python reserved keyword.

tools.description:
Auto-layout a specific subset of nodes in a graph.
Uses the same topological-sort layering as auto_layout_graph but only repositions
the nodes whose GUIDs are listed in NodeIds — all other nodes are untouched.

NodeIds come from node_id fields returned by get_selected_nodes() or get_nodes_in_graph().

Python Usage:
  # Layout whatever is currently selected in the editor
  selected = unreal.BlueprintService.get_selected_nodes("/Game/BP_Player")
  ids = [n.node_id for n in selected]
  unreal.BlueprintService.auto_layout_selected_nodes("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", ids)

  # Layout a hand-picked list of nodes by GUID
  unreal.BlueprintService.auto_layout_selected_nodes(
      "/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph",
      ["GUID-A", "GUID-B", "GUID-C"])

tools.description:
Auto-layout all nodes in an existing graph.
Uses topological sort on execution flow + layered positioning.
Does not modify any connections or node logic — only positions.

tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AutoLayoutGraph

tools.description:
Measure the visual quality of a graph's current layout WITHOUT changing it.
Returns a JSON report with: nodeCount, wireCount, execWireCount, nodeOverlaps
(+ overlappingPairs), wireCrossings, backwardExecWires (+ list), longWires,
total/avg wire length, execWireMeanAbsDeltaY (0 = perfectly straight exec
backbone), graph bounds, an "issues" summary array (empty = layout looks
clean), and per-node bounding boxes {id, title, x, y, width, height} so an
agent can audit and correct placement.

Intended loop: build_graph(auto_layout=True) → analyze_graph_layout → if
"issues" is non-empty, fix (auto_layout_selected_nodes / set_node_position)
and re-check. Comment boxes are ignored (decoration, not structure).

Python Usage (bool return is folded away — the two out-strings come back as a tuple):
  report, err = unreal.BlueprintService.analyze_graph_layout("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph")
  data = json.loads(report)
  assert data["nodeOverlaps"] == 0 and data["backwardExecWires"] == 0
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AnalyzeGraphLayout

tools.description:
Convenience: call a function off of a Blueprint variable in one shot.

Resolves the variable's type to its owner class, creates a Get node for the
variable and a function-call node for the function, and wires the variable's
output pin into the call's "self" pin. Use this when you would otherwise
compose add_get_variable_node + add_function_call_node + connect_nodes.

The variable must be an object-reference type (UObject subclass). For
inherited variables the owner class is read from the GeneratedClass property,
so this works for variables defined on parent classes too.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddFunctionCallOnVariable

blueprintPath.description: Full path to the blueprint that contains the graph

variableName.description: Variable on this blueprint whose type owns the function

functionName.description: Function to call on the variable's class (e.g. "GetRandomPatrolPoint")

posX.description: X position for the function-call node

posY.description: Y position for the function-call node

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) of the function-call node if successful, empty string otherwise Example: # PatrolPointManager is a BP_PatrolPointManager_C variable on STT_MoveToPatrolPoint call_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_function_call_on_variable( "/Game/StateTree/Tasks/STT_MoveToPatrolPoint", "EventGraph", "PatrolPointManager", "GetRandomPatrolPoint", 400, 100)

tools.description:
Add a parameter to an Event Dispatcher's signature. Parameters become inputs
on the dispatcher's "Call" node and are received by all subscribers.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddEventDispatcherParameter

parameterType.description: Type string (same type-string format as add_function_local_variable)

bIsArray.description: Whether the parameter is an array

returnValue.description: True if successful Example: unreal.BlueprintService.add_event_dispatcher_parameter( "/Game/BP_Player", "OnHealthChanged", "NewHealth", "float")

tools.description:
Add a Blueprint Event Dispatcher (multicast delegate) to a blueprint.
This is the same as clicking "+" under the "Event Dispatchers" section in the
Blueprint editor's My Blueprint panel. Creates both the multicast delegate
member variable AND the signature graph that defines its parameters.

The skeleton class is recompiled immediately so the dispatcher is callable
right after this returns — you do not need to compile the blueprint before
calling add_call_delegate_node.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddEventDispatcher

returnValue.description: True if successful, false if the name already exists or creation failed Example: unreal.BlueprintService.add_event_dispatcher("/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube", "FinishedLooking") # Then to broadcast it: node_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_call_delegate_node( "/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube", "EventGraph", "FinishedLooking", 1400, -700)

tools.description:
Convenience: bind to an event dispatcher declared on a Blueprint variable's class in one shot.

Resolves the variable's type to its owner class (e.g. variable "Cube : BP_Cube_C" -> BP_Cube_C),
finds the named multicast delegate on that class, creates a "Bind Event to <Delegate>" node and
a Get node for the variable, and wires the variable's output pin into the bind node's Target (self).

The variable must be an object-reference type (UObject subclass). For inherited variables the
owner class is read from the GeneratedClass property, so this works for variables defined on
parent classes too.

After calling this you still need to:
  - Wire the bind node's exec input ("execute") from your upstream node
  - Wire a Custom Event's "OutputDelegate" pin into the bind node's "Delegate" pin
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddDelegateBindOnVariable

blueprintPath.description: Full path to the blueprint that contains the graph

variableName.description: Variable on this blueprint whose type owns the event dispatcher

delegateName.description: Multicast delegate (event dispatcher) on the variable's class

posX.description: X position for the bind node

posY.description: Y position for the bind node

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) of the bind node if successful, empty string otherwise Example: # Cube is a BP_Cube_C variable on STT_LookInRandomDirection. # BP_Cube has an event dispatcher "FinishedLooking". bind_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_delegate_bind_on_variable( "/Game/StateTree/Tasks/STT_LookInRandomDirection", "EventGraph", "Cube", "FinishedLooking", 960, 0)

tools.description:
Add a delegate bind node (AddDelegate) to a graph.
This creates the "Bind Event to <DelegateName>" node used to subscribe a function to a multicast delegate.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddDelegateBindNode

targetClass.description: Class that owns the delegate. Accepts: - "Self" or "" for the blueprint's own class - A native class name with or without U/A prefix (e.g. "Actor", "UButton") - A Blueprint asset path (e.g. "/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube") - A short Blueprint name with or without _C suffix (e.g. "BP_Cube", "BP_Cube_C")

delegateName.description: Name of the multicast delegate property (e.g. "OnActorBeginOverlap")

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) if successful, empty string otherwise Example: node_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_delegate_bind_node("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", "Self", "OnDamageTaken", 200, 100) node_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_delegate_bind_node("/Game/WBP_HUD", "EventGraph", "UButton", "OnClicked", 300, 200) node_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_delegate_bind_node("/Game/STT_LookAt", "EventGraph", "BP_Cube", "FinishedLooking", 960, 0)

tools.description:
Add a Custom Event node to a graph.
This creates the same event-style node exposed by the Blueprint editor's
"Add Custom Event..." action and returns the resulting node GUID.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddCustomEventNode

eventName.description: Desired custom event name. Leave empty to let Unreal pick a unique name.

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) if successful, empty string otherwise Example: node_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_custom_event_node("/Game/STT_Rotate", "EventGraph", "OnTimerFinished", 600, 0)

tools.description:
Add an input parameter (user-defined input pin) to an existing Custom Event node.
This is the equivalent of clicking "+ New Parameter" under Inputs in the Details panel
with a Custom Event node selected. The node is identified by its GUID (as returned by
add_custom_event_node / get_nodes_in_graph).
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddCustomEventInput

graphName.description: Name of the graph containing the node (e.g. "EventGraph")

nodeId.description: GUID of the Custom Event node

parameterName.description: Name of the new input pin

parameterType.description: Type string (same type-string format as add_function_local_variable, e.g. "float", "FRotator", "AActor")

bIsArray.description: Whether the parameter is an array

returnValue.description: True if the pin was added Example: unreal.BlueprintService.add_custom_event_input("/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube", "EventGraph", node_id, "Rotation", "FRotator")

tools.description:
Add a Create Event node (implemented as UK2Node_CreateDelegate) to a graph.
Use this for delegate workflows where a function name must be converted into a delegate value.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddCreateEventNode

functionName.description: Optional function name to preselect on the node. Leave empty to add an unconfigured node.

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) if successful, empty string otherwise Example: node_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_create_event_node("/Game/STT_Rotate", "EventGraph", "OnTimerFinished", 300, 0)

tools.description:
Add a "Create Event" node (K2Node_CreateDelegate) to a graph.
This wraps a named function as a delegate reference, for connection to the
Delegate pin of a Bind Event node (add_delegate_bind_node).
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddCreateDelegateNode

functionName.description: Name of the function (must match the delegate signature)

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) if successful, empty string otherwise Example: create_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_create_delegate_node("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", "OnVibeEventReceived", 200, -150) unreal.BlueprintService.connect_nodes("/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", create_id, "OutputDelegate", bind_id, "Delegate")

tools.description: Add a component to a blueprint.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddComponent

parentName.description: Optional name of parent component (for scene components)

returnValue.description: True if successful Example - Add a static mesh: unreal.BlueprintService.add_component("/Game/BP_Player", "StaticMeshComponent", "Body") Example - Add with parent: unreal.BlueprintService.add_component("/Game/BP_Player", "SpotLightComponent", "HeadLight", "Head")

tools.description:
Add a Comment box (UEdGraphNode_Comment) to a graph at an explicit position and size.
Comment boxes are the yellow/coloured bubbles that visually group nodes. By default
any K2 nodes whose bounds fall inside the comment box will be picked up and dragged
with the comment (GroupMovement mode), matching the standard editor behaviour when
the user creates a comment via the C hotkey.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddCommentNode

graphName.description: Name of the graph (e.g. "EventGraph", or a function name)

commentText.description: Text displayed in the comment header

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) of the new comment node, empty string on failure. Example: cid = unreal.BlueprintService.add_comment_node( "/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", "Damage handling", 100.0, 50.0, 600.0, 300.0, 1.0, 0.95, 0.4, 0.4)

tools.description:
Add a Comment box that wraps the supplied nodes. The position and size are computed
from the bounding box of the listed nodes, plus the requested padding. This is the
programmatic equivalent of selecting nodes in the editor and pressing C.

Pair this with `get_selected_nodes()` to wrap whatever the user has highlighted in
the open Blueprint editor:

  sel = unreal.BlueprintService.get_selected_nodes("/Game/BP_Player")
  ids = [n.node_id for n in sel]
  unreal.BlueprintService.add_comment_around_nodes(
      "/Game/BP_Player", "EventGraph", "Damage handling", ids)
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddCommentAroundNodes

graphName.description: Name of the graph that contains the nodes

commentText.description: Text displayed in the comment header

nodeIds.description: GUIDs of the nodes to wrap (as returned by get_selected_nodes / get_nodes_in_graph)

padding.description: Padding around the bounding box in graph units (default 40)

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) of the new comment node, empty string on failure (e.g. no valid node IDs found in the graph).

tools.description:
Add a "Call <Dispatcher>" node (UK2Node_CallDelegate) to a graph.
This is the broadcast node — wire the execution flow into its "execute" pin
to fire all subscribers of the dispatcher.
tools.name: VibeUE.BlueprintService.AddCallDelegateNode

blueprintPath.description: Full path to the blueprint that owns the dispatcher

graphName.description: Name of the graph to place the node in (e.g. "EventGraph")

dispatcherName.description: Name of the event dispatcher to call

returnValue.description: Node ID (GUID) if successful, empty string otherwise Example: node_id = unreal.BlueprintService.add_call_delegate_node( "/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube", "EventGraph", "FinishedLooking", 1400, -700) unreal.BlueprintService.connect_nodes( "/Game/StateTree/BP_Cube", "EventGraph", timeline_id, "Finished", node_id, "execute")
